text:
mike: Quick heads-up — I captured a full Nsight trace for the 8-GPU shard run to investigate the perf regression from last night. Capture size ~4GB. Patterns look suspicious around the KV cache warmup + first few decode steps.
sara: Nice. Was this the tensor-parallel + pipeline-parallel config (tp=2, pp=4)? :thinking:
mike: Yep tp=2 pp=4, model=redwood-34B-quant. We saw median token latency jump ~25% when sequence length > 2048.
jun: Do you have nvprof/ncu summary too? Nsight is great but nvprof gives quick kernel timeline numbers we can diff.
mike: I ran ncu with --target-overview and nvprof-style sampling. Summary:
```
GPU0 compute  68%  | comm 24% | idle 8%
GPU1 compute  45%  | comm 48% | idle 7%
... (similar skew across ranks)
All-reduce (NCCL) shows spikes that block compute on PP stage boundaries.
```
sara: That per-GPU skew suggests imbalanced pipeline fill + synchronous all-reduce at certain layers. Could be our KV cache alignment forcing sync points.
alexa: I remember we had a KV cache optimization that pads to a multiple of 256 tokens to improve kernel launch sizes. That can shift layer boundaries between ranks. If one rank hits an all-reduce earlier it stalls others.
jun: Idea: instrument custom timers around communication and key cache access to get exact overlap numbers instead of inferring from traces. Something like:
```
// pseudo
start_compute = wall_clock();
launch_forward_layer();
cudaEventRecord(evt1, stream_compute);
ncclAllReduce(..., comm_stream);
cudaEventRecord(evt2, stream_comm);
// later
cudaEventSynchronize(evt1/evt2);
compute_ms = elapsed(evt1, evt_sync);
comm_ms = elapsed(evt2, evt_sync);
```
mike: I added lightweight host timers + per-stream CUDA events. Early results show ~120ms wasted waiting on all-reduce in the first 8 decode steps (KV warmup) even though kernel exec on other stream had work. So comm/compute overlap isn't effective during warmup.
sara: Could be NCCL using default stream ordering which serializes with compute stream. Try NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME or setting NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR=1? Also check if we set CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING accidentally in the run.
jun: Also check if our NCCL ops are launched on a different stream but with the same CUDA event ordering causing implicit sync. We should ensure comm_stream is created with cudaStreamNonBlocking and we never call cudaEventSynchronize on compute stream until necessary.
alexa: Ops-bot note: I captured topology via nvidia-smi topo -m — these hosts have mixed NVLink/PCIe rings; some GPU pairs go over NVLink, others go PCIe which raises variance. That explains some skew between ranks pinned to different nodes.
mike: Action plan I proposed: 1) Add per-layer comm/compute timers (host+events) and export as CSV. 2) Run a short synthetic with fixed seq len 256/1024/2048 to isolate KV padding effect. 3) Try launching NCCL ops on nonblocking streams + set NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE=GROUP to improve overlap. 4) For baseline, measure token-level SLO with batching turned off to see per-token cost.
sara: For batching heuristics: we noticed large batches created at kv-warmup cause long tail on first token. Maybe prioritize small immediate batches for first N tokens, then enable larger batching. Put a KV-warmup mode that disables aggressive coalescing for the first 16 tokens.
jun: Agree. Also kernel selection: if we pick an attention kernel optimized for long sequences that increases per-step compute time and pushes comms into critical path. We should compare kernel A (loop-optimized) vs kernel B (memory-optimized) and pick per-layer based on seq length. Add per-kernel perf counters in the trace.
mike: I uploaded the Nsight capture to /internal/perf/traces/1760001234_nsight.zip and a diff script:
```
python perf/diff_trace.py --before b.zip --after a.zip --out csv
```
alexa: Small experiment results from my run: enabling NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE=PARALLEL reduced wait_on_comm by ~30% but increased GPU memory transient usage; need to check OOM risk.
sara: Let's avoid sweeping all options at once. Jun, can you add the event timers and a parser to compute:
- per-layer compute_ms (median)
- per-layer comm_ms (median)
- overlap_ms = max(0, compute_window - comm_window overlapping)
- parallel_efficiency = compute_ms / (compute_ms + comm_ms - overlap_ms)
Exported CSV should have columns: layer, step, gpu_rank, compute_ms, comm_ms, overlap_ms, kernel_name.
jun: On it, will push a small PR for the timers + CSV emitter today.
mike: I'll coordinate the synthetic runs and upload raw nvprof/ncu summaries. If we confirm KV padding is culprit, we'll change padding to align windows by PP stage not a global 256.
alexa: Also put a perf regression alert in the console: if median token-latency for >=1024 seq increases by >15% vs baseline, auto-roll back to previous kernel selection.
sara: Good call. Perf-bot: create an alert ticket? :point_down:
perf-bot: created perf-6372 (Regression alert rule + dashboard panels) :white_check_mark:
mike: Thanks. Let's re-check in this thread once we have the CSVs and short synthetic numbers. Short notes ok in thread. :thumbsup:
